sections.subtitle: „Ljudina“ s mnogo epiteta: Ivan Pokupec gost druge epizode Redefinicije
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj Kruno predstavlja gosta Ivana Pokupca i nabraja njegove epitete
sections.content:
Druga epizoda podcasta **Redefinicija** na kanalu *Muževni budite* otvara se katoličkim pozdravom: „Hvaljen Isus i Marija i sveti Josip!“ Voditelj Kruno potom predstavlja gosta, **Ivana Pokupca**, kojeg opisuje kao „zanimljiv lik“ i „ljudinu“.

Kruno nabraja niz epiteta koji prate njegova sugovornika:
- aktivist,
- javni zagovornik vrijednosti braka, života i obitelji,
- „kontroverzni vjeroučitelj“.

Voditelj naglašava da je epiteta mnogo i da će se nekih tijekom razgovora dotaknuti. Pokupec zahvaljuje na pozivu i u šali dodaje da su neki drugi epiteti zanimljiviji te da će o njima biti riječi „along the way“. Tim tonom, opuštenim, ali i otvoreno provokativnim, započinje razgovor koji će obuhvatiti aktivizam, politiku, školstvo, očinstvo, feminizam i javno svjedočenje vjere.
sections.subtitle_en: “A great man” with many epithets: Ivan Pokupec guest of the second episode of Redefinicija
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host Kruno introduces guest Ivan Pokupec and lists his epithets
sections.content_en:
The second episode of the podcast **Redefinicija** on the channel *Muževni budite* opens with the Catholic greeting: “Praised be Jesus and Mary and Saint Joseph!” Host Kruno then introduces the guest, **Ivan Pokupec**, whom he describes as an “interesting character” and “a great man”.

Kruno lists a series of epithets that accompany his interlocutor:
- activist,
- public advocate for the values of marriage, life, and family,
- “controversial religion teacher”.

The host emphasizes that there are many epithets and that they will touch upon some of them during the conversation. Pokupec thanks him for the invitation and jokingly adds that some other epithets are more interesting and that they will be discussed “along the way”. In that tone, relaxed, but also openly provocative, begins the conversation that will cover activism, politics, education, fatherhood, feminism, and public witness of faith.

sections.subtitle: Sve je počelo na parkiralištu: od „sebičnog“ okidača do humanitarnog aktivizma
sections.screenshot_description: Ivan Pokupec opisuje problem s parkiranjem iza zgrade KBF-a u Vlaškoj
sections.content:
Na pitanje što je bio okidač njegova društvenog angažmana, Ivan Pokupec iskreno odgovara da su to bili **„sebični razlozi“**. Godine 2005. upisao je Katehetski institut na Katoličkom bogoslovnom fakultetu, smješten u Vlaškoj, u samom središtu Zagreba. Onamo je svakodnevno putovao iz Velike Gorice, a predavanja su ponekad trajala od jutra do kasnog poslijepodneva. Parkiranje mu je zato postalo velik problem.

Iza zgrade KBF-a isprva se nalazio raskopani prostor, gotovo gradilište, na kojem se moglo slobodno parkirati. Pokupec ga opisuje kao prostor između KBF-a i zgrade Nacionala, gdje će, kako navodi, dvije godine kasnije biti počinjen atentat na Pukanića. Kada je ondje uređeno službeno parkiralište koje se naplaćivalo, mladi student „bez love“ našao se u nevolji.

Tada je primijetio da su rijetka žuta parkirna mjesta za osobe s invaliditetom u centru grada u pravilu zauzeta „divljim markama automobila“ bez ikakve oznake da ih vozi osoba s invaliditetom. Kako sam kaže, aktivizam mu je počeo pitanjem kako riješiti vlastiti problem, a zatim i problem ostalih osoba s invaliditetom pri parkiranju u središtu Zagreba. Prvi aktivistički koraci tako su ga doveli u sukob sa Zagreb parkingom, odnosno s pokojnim gospodinom Bandićem.

Kada je taj problem riješio, aktivizam se proširio na **djecu s teškoćama u razvoju** i poprimio humanitarni karakter. Pokupec govori o „desecima, stotinama akcija“ za djecu s teškoćama u razvoju i osobe s invaliditetom, kojima je stekao određeni studentski renome. Sazrijevanjem je, međutim, shvatio da je i humanitarni aktivizam dobrim dijelom **„jedan veliki, ponekad i prljavi biznis“**. Nakon toga se na nekoliko godina povukao iz aktivizma.

Ponovno ga je, kako kaže, „čisto zbog emocije“ pokrenuo prizor dramatičnih deložacija 2015. godine, kada ulazi u politički aktivizam. Ističe da uvijek kasni u sazrijevanjima. Danas svoj aktivizam smatra možda najslobodnijim dosad jer više nije vezan ni uz jednu organizaciju niti o ikome financijski ovisi. Aktivizmom se, kaže, bavi „sebi za gušt“, u slobodno vrijeme, i može slobodno reći što misli.

sections.subtitle_en: Everything started in a parking lot: from a „selfish“ trigger to humanitarian activism
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Pokupec describes the parking problem behind the KBF building in Vlaška
sections.content_en:
To the question of what was the trigger of his social engagement, Ivan Pokupec honestly answers that these were **„selfish reasons“**. In 2005, he enrolled in the Katehetski institut at the Katolički bogoslovni fakultet, located in Vlaška, in the very center of Zagreb. He traveled there daily from Velika Gorica, and lectures sometimes lasted from morning until late afternoon. Parking therefore became a big problem for him.

Behind the KBF building there was initially a dug-up area, almost a construction site, where one could park freely. Pokupec describes it as the space between the KBF and the Nacional building, where, as he states, two years later the assassination of Pukanić would be committed. When an official paid parking lot was arranged there, the young student „without money“ found himself in trouble.

Then he noticed that the rare yellow parking spaces for persons with disabilities in the city center were as a rule occupied by „wild car brands“ without any indication that a person with disabilities was driving them. As he says himself, his activism began with the question of how to solve his own problem, and then also the problem of other persons with disabilities when parking in the center of Zagreb. His first activist steps thus brought him into conflict with Zagreb parking, that is, with the late Mr. Bandić.

When he solved that problem, the activism expanded to **children with developmental difficulties** and took on a humanitarian character. Pokupec speaks of „dozens, hundreds of actions“ for children with developmental difficulties and persons with disabilities, through which he gained a certain student reputation. By maturing, however, he realized that humanitarian activism is also largely **„one big, sometimes dirty business“**. After that, he withdrew from activism for several years.

He was moved again, as he says, „purely because of emotion“, by the sight of dramatic evictions in 2015, when he entered political activism. He points out that he is always late in maturing. Today he considers his activism perhaps the freest so far because he is no longer tied to any organization nor does he depend financially on anyone. He engages in activism, he says, „for his own pleasure“, in his free time, and he can freely say what he thinks.
keywords_en: parking spaces for persons with disabilities

sections.subtitle: Živi zid i Slobodna Hrvatska: ponos bez žaljenja, ali i lekcija za budućnost
sections.screenshot_description: Ivan Pokupec govori o izlasku oko 150 članova iz Živog zida i osnivanju Slobodne Hrvatske
sections.content:
Kruno zatim pita gosta kako se danas osvrće na sudjelovanje u političkim opcijama **Živi zid** i **Slobodna Hrvatska** te žali li zbog toga. Odgovor je kratak: ne žali.

Pokupec je Živom zidu pristupio početkom 2015., a napustio ga je krajem iste godine. Ušao je prvenstveno kao aktivist, „kupljen“ emocijom koju su u njemu izazvali dramatični prizori deložacija. Naglašava da nije imao političkih ambicija i da se uključio srcem, iz današnje perspektive „možda i previše“. Unutar stranke brzo je napredovao, kako kaže, zbog razine pismenosti i obrazovanja koju je imao.

Upravo mu je to pomoglo da relativno brzo prepozna **„smicalice i podvale“** na političkoj strani priče u Živom zidu. Krajem 2015. oko 150 članova kolektivno je izašlo iz stranke i osnovalo Slobodnu Hrvatsku. Pokupec ističe razliku: u Živom zidu bili su članovi, a u novoj stranci osnivači. Slobodna Hrvatska nastavila je, prema njegovim riječima, sa sličnim programskim smjernicama.

Na pitanje o žaljenju odlučno odgovara: **„Niti malo, apsolutno.“** Ponosan je na svoju ulogu, kako god priča završila. Priznaje ipak da to danas vjerojatno ne bi ponovio, zbog „vrlo prizemnog“ načina na koji je sve završilo. Namjere su, kaže, bile časne, iskrene i dobre, a unutar tih političkih opcija mnogo je toga dobroga napravio i naučio.
sections.subtitle_en: Živi zid and Slobodna Hrvatska: pride without regret, but also a lesson for the future
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Pokupec speaks about the departure of about 150 members from Živi zid and the founding of Slobodna Hrvatska
sections.content_en:
Kruno then asks the guest how he looks back today on his participation in the political options **Živi zid** and **Slobodna Hrvatska**, and whether he regrets it. The answer is brief: he does not regret it.

Pokupec joined Živi zid in early 2015, and left it at the end of the same year. He entered primarily as an activist, „bought“ by the emotion stirred in him by dramatic scenes of evictions. He emphasizes that he had no political ambitions and that he got involved with his heart, from today's perspective „perhaps even too much.“ Within the party he advanced quickly, as he says, due to the level of literacy and education he had.

That is precisely what helped him relatively quickly recognize the **„tricks and setups“** on the political side of the story in Živi zid. At the end of 2015, about 150 members collectively left the party and founded Slobodna Hrvatska. Pokupec emphasizes the difference: in Živi zid they were members, while in the new party they were founders. Slobodna Hrvatska continued, according to his words, with similar programmatic guidelines.

To the question about regret he responds decisively: **„Not in the least, absolutely.“** He is proud of his role, however the story ended. He admits, nonetheless, that he probably would not repeat it today, because of the „very base“ way in which everything ended. The intentions, he says, were honorable, sincere, and good, and within those political options he did and learned a lot of good things.

sections.subtitle: „Gradili smo kuću od krova“: duhovno probuđenje kao preduvjet društvene promjene
sections.screenshot_description: Ivan Pokupec objašnjava metaforu kuće koja se gradi od temelja, a ne od krova
sections.content:
Na temelju političkog iskustva Kruno pita je li društvena promjena moguća samo političkim angažmanom. Pokupec danas zastupa suprotno stajalište: promjena je, prema njegovu mišljenju, moguća **isključivo na neki drugi način**.

Objašnjava to slikovitom metaforom. Sve političke i aktivističke opcije u kojima je sudjelovao, kaže, zapravo su **„gradile kuću od krova umjesto od temelja“**. Danas je uvjeren da je preduvjet za sve duhovno probuđenje, duhovna i psihološka promjena među ljudima kao narodom. Politička promjena, smatra, tek će uslijediti kao posljedica toga, a ne obrnuto, jer „kuću treba graditi od temelja, a ne odozgora“.
sections.subtitle_en: "We Were Building the House from the Roof": Spiritual Awakening as a Prerequisite for Social Change
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Pokupec explains the metaphor of a house being built from the foundation, not from the roof
sections.content_en:
Based on political experience, Kruno asks whether social change is possible only through political engagement. Today Pokupec holds the opposite view: change is, in his opinion, possible **exclusively in some other way**.

He explains this with a vivid metaphor. All the political and activist options in which he participated, he says, were actually **"building the house from the roof instead of from the foundation"**. Today he is convinced that the prerequisite for everything is spiritual awakening, a spiritual and psychological change among people as a people. Political change, he believes, will only follow as a consequence of that, and not vice versa, because "a house should be built from the foundation, and not from above".

sections.subtitle: Učionica kao temelj: od „woke“ gradova do imotskih obitelji s troje i četvero djece
sections.screenshot_description: Ivan Pokupec uspoređuje kulturu velikih gradova s kulturom koju je vidio u Imotskom
sections.content:
Kruno nastavlja na metaforu i pita kako Pokupec kao vjeroučitelj u učionici gradi „kuću od temelja do krova“. Gost odgovara da iskorištava svaki mogući prostor kako bi **oblikovao „male umove“** na ispravan način i u ispravnoj kulturi.

Putujući Hrvatskom, kaže, uočava velike kulturološke krajnosti. S jedne su strane urbane sredine i veliki gradovi koji se, prema njegovim riječima, „guše u toj woke filozofiji“ i u, kako voli reći, **„leftarskim narativima“**. S druge je strane iskustvo s ovogodišnjeg, kako kaže, poluturističkog boravka u **Imotskom**, gdje je vidio „dijametralno suprotnu“ kulturu:
- dijete se doživljava kao blagoslov,
- pobačaj se uopće ne uzima u obzir kao opcija,
- mladi ljudi u dvadesetima i ranim tridesetima imaju troje ili četvero djece,
- obitelji se grade na zdravim vrijednostima i temeljima.

Kao vjeroučitelj, a radio je, ističe, sa svim uzrastima, od najmanjih do srednjoškolaca, uvijek se trudio usaditi učenicima zdrave vrijednosti. Svjestan je da ne može kontrolirati kako će se one dalje razvijati u njihovim životima. Ipak, zna iz vlastitog iskustva da je i sam postao vjeroučitelj zahvaljujući svom vjeroučitelju iz osnovne škole, čije se posađeno sjeme kasnije razvilo i razgranalo u njegovu životu. Zato, kaže, pokušava učiniti isto što je činio njegov **Stipo Bilić**, kojemu usput upućuje „veliki pozdrav“.
sections.subtitle_en: The classroom as a foundation: from "woke" cities to Imotski families with three and four children
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Pokupec compares the culture of big cities with the culture he saw in Imotski
sections.content_en:
Kruno builds on the metaphor and asks how Pokupec, as a catechist in the classroom, builds "a house from the foundation to the roof". The guest responds that he utilizes every possible space to **shape "little minds"** in the right way and in the right culture.

Traveling through Croatia, he says, he observes great cultural extremes. On one side are urban environments and large cities that, according to his words, "are suffocating in that woke philosophy" and in, as he likes to say, **"leftist narratives"**. On the other side is the experience from this year's, as he says, semi-tourist stay in **Imotski**, where he saw a "diametrically opposite" culture:
- a child is perceived as a blessing,
- abortion is not considered an option at all,
- young people in their twenties and early thirties have three or four children,
- families are built on healthy values and foundations.

As a catechist—and he has worked, he points out, with all age groups, from the youngest to high schoolers—he has always tried to instill healthy values in students. He is aware that he cannot control how they will develop further in their lives. Still, he knows from his own experience that he himself became a catechist thanks to his elementary school catechist, whose planted seed later developed and branched out in his life. That is why, he says, he tries to do the same thing his **Stipo Bilić** did, to whom he sends "a big greeting" in passing.

sections.subtitle: Uhljebnički sustav i škola bez odgoja: zašto je vjeronauk ostao „luksuzna pozicija“
sections.screenshot_description: Ivan Pokupec govori o nestanku odgojne uloge iz školskih predmeta osim vjeronauka
sections.content:
S obzirom na gotovo dva desetljeća iskustva u obrazovnom sustavu, Kruno pita koji su danas najveći izazovi u školstvu i što bi Pokupec promijenio. Gost izdvaja **dvije stvari**.

**Prva je uhljebnički karakter sustava.** Prema njegovim riječima, školstvo je samim ustrojem „podosta uhljebničko“ jer privlači ljude koji nisu previše motivirani. Posao nudi relativnu ugodu i sigurnost, a plaća je na kraju mjeseca ista, bez obzira na to daje li netko od sebe sto ili deset posto. To smatra negativnim, jer sustav privlači ljude koji traže „ziherašku“ sigurnost.

**Druga je nestanak odgojne uloge.** Kroz godine se, objašnjava, odgojni element izgubio iz većine predmeta, osim iz vjeronauka. Upozorava da ljudi to ne shvaćaju kad se pred izbore otvore priče o vatikanskim ugovorima i micanju vjeronauka iz škola. Kad je on bio dijete, svaki je profesor djelovao i odgojno. Danas je, kaže, nastava u učionici i kurikulumu toliko regulirana da je nastavnik vrlo ograničen.

Vjeronauk je, prema njegovu mišljenju, jedini predmet koji je ostao **odgojno-obrazovni, a ne obrazovno-odgojni**. To naziva „luksuznom pozicijom“ koja vjeroučiteljima još uvijek omogućuje odgojno djelovanje. Kao primjer navodi vlastito djetinjstvo, kada ga je „bez problema u red dovela profesorica iz matematike“, što se danas, kaže, vidi vrlo rijetko. Danas se još samo vjeroučitelji i vjeroučiteljice bave onim što bi Grci nazvali ljepotom duše, dok je sve ostalo, zaključuje, „nekako postalo robotika“.
sections.subtitle_en: A clientelist system and a school without upbringing: why religious education remained a "luxurious position"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Pokupec speaks about the disappearance of the educational and formative role from school subjects other than religious education
sections.content_en:
Considering almost two decades of experience in the educational system, Kruno asks what the greatest challenges in schooling are today and what Pokupec would change. The guest singles out **two things**.

**The first is the clientelist character of the system.** According to his words, schooling by its very structure is "quite clientelist" because it attracts people who are not overly motivated. The job offers relative comfort and security, and the salary at the end of the month is the same, regardless of whether someone gives one hundred or ten percent of themselves. He considers this negative, because the system attracts people who are looking for "play-it-safe" security.

**The second is the disappearance of the formative role.** Over the years, he explains, the formative element has been lost from most subjects, except from religious education. He warns that people do not realize this when stories about the Vatican agreements and the removal of religious education from schools are opened before elections. When he was a child, every teacher also acted formatively. Today, he says, instruction in the classroom and curriculum is so regulated that the teacher is very limited.

Religious education is, in his opinion, the only subject that remained **formative-educational, rather than educational-formative**. He calls this a "luxurious position" that still allows religious education teachers to act formatively. As an example, he cites his own childhood, when a "mathematics teacher put him in order without any problems," which today, he says, is seen very rarely. Today, only male and female religious education teachers still deal with what the Greeks would call the beauty of the soul, while everything else, he concludes, has "somehow become robotics."

sections.subtitle: „Divljak u redovima“: netipični vjeroučitelj i manjak ratničke energije u Crkvi
sections.screenshot_description: Ivan Pokupec uspoređuje put svetosti blaženog Merza i Ivana Krstitelja
sections.content:
Kako na njegov aktivizam gledaju kolege vjeroučitelji i svećenici? „Šareno, šareno“, odgovara Pokupec. Prema njegovu iskustvu, ljudi ga ili iznimno vole i odobravaju njegov rad ili ga iznimno ne vole, a sredine nema. To, kaže, razumije.

Sebe opisuje kao **„apsolutno netipičnog vjeroučitelja“**. Tipičnog vjeroučitelja zamišlja kao osobu koja voli monokromatske boje u odjeći, koja je plašljiva, mirna, staložena i „svetački raspoložena“. Takvim se ljudima, kaže, oduvijek divio, jer je njegov karakter potpuno suprotan. Zato mu nije čudno da takve ljude smeta „jedan divljak u njihovim redovima“ poput njega.

Dugo mu je trebalo, priznaje, da shvati kako su **putovi do svetosti različiti** i da je Bog ljude namjerno stvorio različitih karaktera. Put do svetosti može voditi preko blaženog Merza, ali i preko Ivana Krstitelja. „Obojica su Ivani“, dodaje.

Pokupec smatra da Crkvi, kao zajednici vjernika, često nedostaje **muževnije, ratničke energije**. Napominje da ga se ne shvati krivo, ali smatra da je katolička vjera u Hrvatskoj „feminizirana“ i da se poistovjećuje sa „starim bakicama koje okreću krunicu po cijele dane“. Pita gdje je u svemu tome „muški ratnički moment“ i vjeruje da u tom smislu možda čini nešto dobro, što će, kaže, pokazati vrijeme.

Kruno primjećuje da ga upravo zbog toga zovu „kontroverznim vjeroučiteljem“. Pokupec odgovara da je taj naziv došao od novinara, ali da se ustalio. Kruno zaključuje da se „zalijepio“.
sections.subtitle_en: “A savage in the ranks”: an atypical religion teacher and the lack of warrior energy in the Church
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Pokupec compares the path to holiness of Blessed Merz and John the Baptist
sections.content_en:
How do fellow religion teachers and priests view his activism? “Mixed, mixed,” Pokupec responds. According to his experience, people either love him immensely and approve of his work or intensely dislike him, and there is no middle ground. That, he says, he understands.

He describes himself as an **“absolutely atypical religion teacher”**. He imagines a typical religion teacher as a person who likes monochromatic colors in clothing, who is timid, calm, composed, and “saintly disposed.” He has always admired such people, he says, because his character is completely the opposite. That is why it is not strange to him that such people are bothered by “a savage in their ranks” like him.

It took him a long time, he admits, to realize that the **paths to holiness are different** and that God intentionally created people with different characters. The path to holiness can lead through Blessed Merz, but also through John the Baptist. “Both are Ivans,” he adds.

Pokupec believes that the Church, as a community of believers, often lacks **more masculine, warrior energy**. He notes not to be misunderstood, but he considers the Catholic faith in Croatia to be “feminized” and equated with “old grannies turning the Rosary all day long.” He asks where the “male warrior moment” is in all of that and believes that in that sense he might be doing something good, which, he says, time will tell.

Kruno observes that it is precisely because of this that they call him a “controversial religion teacher.” Pokupec replies that this title came from journalists, but that it took root. Kruno concludes that it “stuck.”

sections.subtitle: Dječje sudbine koje se ne zaboravljaju i poruka bez zadrške: bez Krista nema spasenja
sections.screenshot_description: Ivan Pokupec govori o Kristu kao Janjetu, ali i Lavu iz Judina plemena
sections.content:
Kruno pita što se Pokupcu najviše urezalo u pamćenje u radu s djecom. Gost se poziva na zajedničko iskustvo, jer je i Kruno bio profesor: nastavnik najduže pamti najproblematičnije i najbolje učenike. Pokupcu su ipak najviše ostali u sjećanju učenici koji akademski nisu bili ni najbolji ni najlošiji, nego oni čije su ga **životne situacije osobno dotaknule**.

Kao nastavnik, kaže, „nagledaš se svega“, pa i djece kojima je nastavnik u dva školska sata tjedno više otac nego njihovi očevi kod kuće. Sluša se i tragičnih priča koje nijedno dijete ne bi smjelo proživljavati. To ga, priznaje, ne može ostaviti ravnodušnim: ponekad poželi svu tu djecu zagrliti, privinuti k sebi i zaštititi da ih „nitko krivo ni ne pogleda“. Najviše pamti upravo teške i nepravedne dječje sudbine, a u ta mala djetinjstva najviše je i nastojao uložiti sebe.

Na pitanje koju vrijednost najviše želi prenijeti učenicima, odgovara da je to istina da je **Krist spasitelj i kralj**, da je Janje, ali i **Lav iz Judina plemena** te gospodar nad vojskama. Krist, kaže, nije samo očinski nježna figura, „što je Bogu hvala“, nego i pravedna figura koja donosi ratničku energiju i duhovnu pobjedu kakva je ljudima često potrebna.

Pokupec smatra da se danas izgubila iz vida temeljna istina da **bez Krista nema spasenja**. U atmosferi političke korektnosti, kaže, vjernici se boje to i izgovoriti. Društvo u kojemu sve veću ulogu imaju druge religije, ateizam, odnosno antiteizam, i katolička „pristojnost“ dovode do toga da se ta velika istina prešućuje. Zaključuje da je vrijeme da se ona vrati, u ljubavi, ali tako da se svakome „jasno u facu“ kaže da bez Isusa nema spasenja.
sections.subtitle_en: Children's fates that are not forgotten and a message without reservation: without Christ there is no salvation
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Pokupec speaks about Christ as the Lamb, but also the Lion of the tribe of Judah
sections.content_en:
Kruno asks what was most etched into Pokupec's memory in his work with children. The guest refers to a shared experience, because Kruno was also a teacher: a teacher remembers the most problematic and the best students the longest. However, the students who remained most in Pokupec's memory were those who academically were neither the best nor the worst, but those whose **life situations personally touched him**.

As a teacher, he says, "you see everything," including children to whom a teacher in two school hours a week is more of a father than their fathers at home. One also listens to tragic stories that no child should have to experience. That, he admits, cannot leave him indifferent: sometimes he wishes to hug all those children, hold them close to himself, and protect them so that "no one even looks at them the wrong way." He remembers precisely the difficult and unjust children's fates the most, and it was into those small childhoods that he sought the most to invest himself.

To the question of which value he most wants to convey to students, he answers that it is the truth that **Christ is savior and king**, that he is the Lamb, but also the **Lion of the tribe of Judah** and the lord of hosts. Christ, he says, is not only a paternally gentle figure, "which is, thank God," but also a just figure who brings warrior energy and spiritual victory of the kind people often need.

Pokupec considers that today the fundamental truth that **without Christ there is no salvation** has been lost from sight. In an atmosphere of political correctness, he says, believers are afraid to even say it out loud. A society in which other religions, atheism, or rather antitheism, and Catholic "politeness" play an increasingly large role leads to this great truth being silenced. He concludes that it is time for it to be brought back, in love, but in such a way that everyone is told "clearly to their face" that without Jesus there is no salvation.
entities_en: Lion of the tribe of Judah

sections.subtitle: Najveća prijetnja djeci nisu ekrani, nego nezainteresirani roditelji
sections.screenshot_description: Ivan Pokupec objašnjava da je najveća prijetnja djeci nepažnja roditelja
sections.content:
Kruno podsjeća da je Pokupec otac dvoje djece, a gost dodaje da će ih, ako Bog da, biti još. Voditelj spominje i njegovu „duhovnu djecu“, učenike kojima je predavao i predaje. Pita što je danas najveća prijetnja djeci i njihovu nevinom djetinjstvu.

Odgovor je jasan: **nepažnja roditelja**, „da ne kažem nezainteresiranost“. Pokupec pritom svjesno izbjegava uobičajenu priču o ekranima. Ekran je, kaže, sredstvo kao i sve drugo, a sve što ljudi danas imaju na raspolaganju može biti blagoslov ili prokletstvo, ovisno o tome kako se koristi.

Roditelji, smatra, često griješe jer nisu svjesno uključeni u život djece, nego djeca postaju dio njihove rutine. Ne posvećuju im dovoljno vremena, pažnje i energije, nego se daju odvući vlastitim problemima, rutinama i ekranima, pa se gubi mnogo potencijala.

Prema njegovu iskustvu, gotovo će svako dijete dati onoliko koliko se od njega traži, a današnji se roditelji često boje mnogo tražiti. On sam, kaže, uz puno ljubavi mnogo i zahtijeva od svoje djece, a sve su ljestvice visoko postavljene. Čak i ako ih ne dosegnu, vrijedi izreka: **„pucaj na Mjesec, pa ćeš završiti među zvijezdama“**. Kao roditelj nastoji biti svjesno uključen u sve što djeca rade, imati nadzor nad time i odgajati ih u vrijednostima koje obitelj živi i za koje vjeruje da će im omogućiti kvalitetan život. Zaključuje da u životu svakog djeteta treba više roditeljske koncentracije i pozornosti.
sections.subtitle_en: The greatest threat to children is not screens, but uninterested parents
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Pokupec explains that the greatest threat to children is parental inattention
sections.content_en:
Kruno recalls that Pokupec is a father of two children, and the guest adds that, God willing, there will be more. The host also mentions his "spiritual children", students he taught and teaches. He asks what is the greatest threat to children and their innocent childhood today.

The answer is clear: **parental inattention**, "not to say disinterest". In doing so, Pokupec consciously avoids the usual story about screens. A screen is, he says, a tool like anything else, and everything people have at their disposal today can be a blessing or a curse, depending on how it is used.

Parents, he believes, often make mistakes because they are not consciously involved in their children's lives, but rather children become part of their routine. They do not dedicate enough time, attention, and energy to them, but allow themselves to be distracted by their own problems, routines, and screens, so a lot of potential is lost.

According to his experience, almost every child will give as much as is asked of them, and today's parents are often afraid to ask for much. He himself, he says, along with a lot of love, also demands a lot from his children, and all the bars are set high. Even if they do not reach them, the saying holds true: **"shoot for the Moon, and you will end up among the stars"**. As a parent, he strives to be consciously involved in everything the children do, to have oversight over it, and to raise them in the values that the family lives by and which he believes will enable them to have a quality life. He concludes that in the life of every child there needs to be more parental concentration and attention.

sections.subtitle: Dva lica očinske odsutnosti: posao u inozemstvu i bijeg u kladionice
sections.screenshot_description: Ivan Pokupec govori o očevima koji vrijeme troše na kladionice, alkohol i igrice
sections.content:
Kruno zatim usmjerava razgovor na ulogu oca i pita gdje očevi najviše griješe. Pokupec razlikuje dvije situacije, jednu opravdanu i jednu neopravdanu.

**Prva situacija** odnosi se na očeve koji su zbog posla odsutni iz života svoje djece. Teško je to, kaže, prosuđivati, a kamoli osuđivati. U svojim je učionicama znao imati i do **30 posto učenika** čiji su očevi radili negdje u inozemstvu i nisu bili prisutni jer su pokušavali „staviti kruh na stol“. To ne može osuditi i naziva to „nužnim zlom“.

**Druga situacija** su biološki očevi koje, kako kaže, ne bi ni nazvao očevima u pravom smislu riječi. Oni su se predali hobijima, zadovoljstvima i vlastitim interesima, pa im vrijeme odlazi na:
- kladionice,
- alkohol,
- igrice,
- „gluposti“.

Djeca su tada prepuštena sama sebi jer nedostaje očinska uloga koja, prema Pokupcu, mora značiti **vodstvo, sigurnost i prisutnost**.
sections.subtitle_en: Two faces of fatherly absence: work abroad and escape to betting shops
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Pokupec speaks about fathers who spend their time on betting shops, alcohol, and video games
sections.content_en:
Kruno then directs the conversation to the role of the father and asks where fathers make mistakes the most. Pokupec distinguishes between two situations, one justified and one unjustified.

**The first situation** refers to fathers who are absent from their children's lives due to work. It is difficult, he says, to judge that, let alone condemn it. In his classrooms, he used to have up to **30 percent of students** whose fathers worked somewhere abroad and were not present because they were trying to "put bread on the table." He cannot condemn that and calls it a "necessary evil."

**The second situation** is biological fathers whom, as he says, he would not even call fathers in the true sense of the word. They have surrendered to hobbies, pleasures, and their own interests, so their time goes to:
- betting shops,
- alcohol,
- video games,
- "foolishness."

Children are then left to themselves because the fatherly role is missing, which, according to Pokupec, must mean **leadership, security, and presence**.

sections.subtitle: Radikalni feminizam kao dvosjekli mač: „najveći krivac za pobačaj su muškarci“
sections.screenshot_description: Ivan Pokupec tvrdi da su muškarci najveći krivci za pobačaj
sections.content:
Kruno iznosi mišljenje da su se muškarci danas povukli zbog spomenutih procesa, ali i zbog radikalnog feminizma, jer se boje da će ih drugi smatrati toksičnima ili nametljivima. Pita Pokupca kako gleda na današnji radikalni feminizam, koji, prema voditeljevim riječima, nema veze s izvornim feminizmom.

Pokupec ga naziva **dvosjeklim mačem**. S jedne strane postoji objektivna situacija: kada muškarac ne ispunjava svoju ulogu supruga i oca, žena mora, „htjela-ne htjela“, preuzeti dio te uloge. Prema ženama u takvim okolnostima osjeća veliko suosjećanje. Kada je muškarac, kako se grubo izražava, „bitanga“, žena mora biti i majka i otac jer ju na to prisiljava njegovo ponašanje. Krivnju u tom slučaju s punom odgovornošću pripisuje muškarcu.

Posebno to vrijedi za pitanje pobačaja. **„Za mene najveći krivac za pobačaj danas u svijetu su muškarci“**, ističe Pokupec. Kada muškarac ispunjava ulogu zaštitnika i oslonca, rijetko će se koja žena odlučiti za pobačaj, a to, kaže, i on i Kruno znaju iz osobnog iskustva.

S druge strane postoji situacija u kojoj su se muškarci, u kontekstu radikalnog feminizma, jednostavno dali zastrašiti i povukli se, što nisu smjeli učiniti. Pokupec smatra da su i vjernici možda preozbiljno shvatili feminizam i dali mu previše prostora. Da su ga na vrijeme, kako kaže, „sprdali i ismijali onako kako je trebalo“, vjerojatno se danas ne bi našli u ovoj situaciji.

Zaključuje da svatko tko je proučavao feminizam ili objektivno promatra odnose muškarca i žene shvaća da su oni od pamtivijeka bili **tim**, koji je zajedno gradio život, dom i ispunjavao svoje uloge. U braku, osobito kršćanskom, nema mjesta borbi za dominaciju. Muž i žena tu su da se nadopunjuju, ispunjavaju potrebe jedno drugoga, služe jedno drugome u ljubavi i zajedno podižu dom i djecu. Natjecanje između njih naziva „kratkovidnim i blesavim“ poimanjem odnosa muškarca i žene.
sections.subtitle_en: Radical feminism as a double-edged sword: “the greatest culprit for abortion is men”
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Pokupec claims that men are the greatest culprits for abortion
sections.content_en:
Kruno expresses the opinion that men today have retreated because of the aforementioned processes, but also because of radical feminism, because they fear that others will consider them toxic or intrusive. He asks Pokupec how he views today's radical feminism, which, according to the host's words, has nothing to do with original feminism.

Pokupec calls it a **double-edged sword**. On the one hand, there is an objective situation: when a man does not fulfill his role as husband and father, the woman must, “whether she wants to or not”, take over part of that role. Toward women in such circumstances, he feels great compassion. When a man is, as he crudely puts it, a “scoundrel”, the woman must be both mother and father because his behavior forces her to do so. In that case, he attributes the blame with full responsibility to the man.

This is especially true for the issue of abortion. **“For me, the greatest culprit for abortion in the world today is men”**, Pokupec emphasizes. When a man fulfills the role of protector and support, rarely will any woman decide on an abortion, and that, he says, both he and Kruno know from personal experience.

On the other hand, there is a situation in which men, in the context of radical feminism, simply allowed themselves to be intimidated and retreated, which they should not have done. Pokupec believes that believers, too, perhaps took feminism too seriously and gave it too much space. If they had in time, as he says, “mocked and ridiculed it the way they should have”, they probably would not find themselves in this situation today.

He concludes that anyone who has studied feminism or objectively observes the relations between a man and a woman understands that since time immemorial they were a **team**, which built a life, a home together, and fulfilled their roles. In marriage, especially Christian marriage, there is no place for a struggle for domination. Husband and wife are there to complement each other, fulfill each other's needs, serve each other in love, and raise a home and children together. He calls competition between them a “short-sighted and foolish” conception of the relationship between man and woman.

sections.subtitle: Molitelji i bubnjari na Trgu: mediji, dezinformacije i duhovni autoritet u obitelji
sections.screenshot_description: Ivan Pokupec objašnjava razliku između fizičkog i duhovnog autoriteta u obitelji
sections.content:
Kruno se nadovezuje na krizu muževnosti, pa i ženstvenosti, i navodi kao primjer prve subote na Trgu, gdje ponizni muškarci kleče i mole da budu bolji muževi i očevi. S druge strane, kaže, stoje pretežno žene koje zagovaraju svoja prava, ne razumiju zašto molitelji mole i ne vjeruju u molitvu, ali osjećaju potrebu prosvjedovati i lijepiti im etikete.

Pokupec smatra da su ljudi koji na suprotnoj strani „bubnjaju i vrište i viču i pjena im ide na usta“ ponajprije **zavedeni i dezinformirani** medijima i novinarima. Današnje mainstream medije naziva „najvećom polugom demoniziranosti i zla“, većom od politike i, kako kaže, „oprostiš“, od prostitucije. Smatra da mediji imaju nezamislivu moć da od sveca naprave „najveće dno“ i obrnuto, a informacije koje iz njih dolaze opisuje kao „terorističke“.

Višekratno je, kaže, javno pokušavao upozoriti na razliku između molitve za **fizički autoritet** u obitelji, što, prema njegovu mišljenju, prosvjednici pripisuju moliteljima, i **duhovnog autoriteta**, koji je nešto dijametralno suprotno. Da bi muškarac bio duhovni autoritet u obitelji, objašnjava, mora prije svega biti ponizan i spreman služiti. To nema nikakve veze s autoritetom kakvim ga zamišljaju prosvjednici.

Pokupec podržava molitvena okupljanja na trgovima diljem Hrvatske jer ona muškarcima poručuju: **ostavi se birtije, kladionice i gluposti, posveti se svojoj ženi, djeci i obitelji**. Zato smatra da bi ih svaka feministica, kako se izražava, „sa tri sive stanice u glavi“ trebala prva podržati. Dodaje i nešto što se, prema njegovu mišljenju, u medijima često previdi: prema njegovim zapažanjima, prvim subotama sve se više žena pridružuje muškarcima na Trgu.

Priznaje da kod prosvjednika vjerojatno postoji i politički utjecaj, ali smatra da su „bubnjari“, „zelenokosi i ljubičastokosi“ ponajprije zavedeni. Kada bi u dobroj namjeri pristali na dijalog, molitelji bi im, uvjeren je, brzo objasnili da su im ciljevi zapravo isti. Muškarac koji je duhovni autoritet u obitelji, kaže, „najveći je blagoslov za ženu u toj obitelji“.
sections.subtitle_en: Pray-ers and drummers on the Square: media, misinformation, and spiritual authority in the family
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Pokupec explains the difference between physical and spiritual authority in the family
sections.content_en:
Kruno follows up on the crisis of masculinity, and even femininity, and cites as an example the first Saturdays on the Square, where humble men kneel and pray to be better husbands and fathers. On the other side, he says, stand predominantly women who advocate for their rights, do not understand why the pray-ers pray and do not believe in prayer, but feel the need to protest and attach labels to them.

Pokupec believes that the people who on the opposite side "drum and scream and shout and foam at the mouth" are above all **misled and misinformed** by the media and journalists. He calls today's mainstream media "the greatest lever of demonization and evil", greater than politics and, as he says, "pardon me", than prostitution. He considers that the media have an unimaginable power to make "the lowest scum" out of a saint and vice versa, and he describes the information coming from them as "terrorist".

He has repeatedly, he says, publicly tried to warn about the difference between praying for **physical authority** in the family, which, in his opinion, the protesters attribute to the pray-ers, and **spiritual authority**, which is something diametrically opposite. For a man to be a spiritual authority in the family, he explains, he must above all be humble and ready to serve. That has nothing to do with authority as the protesters imagine it.

Pokupec supports prayer gatherings on squares across Croatia because they send a message to men: **leave the tavern, the betting shop, and nonsense, dedicate yourself to your wife, children, and family**. That is why he believes that every feminist, as he puts it, "with three gray cells in her head" should be the first to support them. He also adds something that, in his opinion, is often overlooked in the media: according to his observations, on first Saturdays more and more women are joining the men on the Square.

He admits that among the protesters there is probably also political influence, but he believes that the "drummers", the "green-haired and purple-haired" are above all misled. If they were to agree in good faith to a dialogue, the pray-ers would, he is convinced, quickly explain to them that their goals are actually the same. A man who is a spiritual authority in the family, he says, is "the greatest blessing for a woman in that family".

sections.subtitle: „Nemamo hrvatsku ljevicu, nego ljevicu u Hrvatskoj“
sections.screenshot_description: Ivan Pokupec objašnjava svoju razliku između hrvatske ljevice i ljevice u Hrvatskoj
sections.content:
Kruno primjećuje da strana preko puta molitelja muževnost doživljava kao prijetnju, možda zbog neugodnih iskustava iz djetinjstva ili odsutnosti uzornog oca, čime se razgovor vraća na krizu očinstva. Iznosi dojam da ta strana želi **„eliminirati oca iz jednadžbe obitelji“**, što se, prema njegovu mišljenju, sustavno događa posljednjih stotinu do dvjesto godina. Ako se ukloni muškarac, obitelj se urušava, a tada država ili bilo tko drugi može s djecom, ženom i obitelji činiti što želi. Pokupec se slaže: „Tako je, nema zaštite.“

Neistomišljenicima Pokupec poručuje dvije stvari. Prva: **vlastite traume ne mogu se izliječiti produbljivanjem trauma drugih**, to nikada nije funkcioniralo niti će. Druga: oni koji vjeruju da muškarci svijetu nisu potrebni, kaže uz dozu ironije, neka pričekaju prvi nestanak struje ili prve veće rupe na cesti.

Feminizam i „ljevičarenje“ općenito naziva neozbiljnom i kratkovidnom političkom i društvenom ideologijom, utemeljenom na parolama koje na prvu dobro zvuče, ali nemaju smisla čim se o njima dublje promisli. Ipak, kaže da može razumjeti idealističnog ljevičara u srednjoj školi ili na fakultetu, kojeg vodi srce i mladenački entuzijazam, što je pozitivno ako je dobro usmjereno.

Problem Hrvatske, prema njegovim riječima, jest to što **nema hrvatsku ljevicu, nego ljevicu u Hrvatskoj**. Hrvatska bi se ljevica, prema tradicionalnoj podjeli političkih uloga, zalagala za hrvatskog radnika, umirovljenika, osobu s invaliditetom i napušteno dijete. Ljevica u Hrvatskoj, kaže, služi drugim interesima, globalističkima, „zastarjelima, jugonacionalističkima“ ili nekim trećima. Ne želi, dodaje, ulaziti u „famozne teorije zavjere“ o Sorosu i masoneriji. Kada ljevica služi interesima koji su bilo čiji osim hrvatskih, dijalog je, smatra, teško ostvariti jer dvije strane nemaju u srcu dobrobit istih ljudi. Jedni žele raditi za Hrvatsku i ljude u njoj, a drugi, zaključuje, služe tuđim interesima, „svjesno ili nesvjesno“.
sections.subtitle_en: "We do not have a Croatian left, but a left in Croatia"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Pokupec explains his distinction between the Croatian left and the left in Croatia
sections.content_en:
Kruno observes that the side across from the prayer intercessors perceives masculinity as a threat, perhaps because of unpleasant childhood experiences or the absence of an exemplary father, which brings the conversation back to the crisis of fatherhood. He expresses the impression that that side wants to **"eliminate the father from the family equation"**, which, in his opinion, has been systematically happening for the last hundred to two hundred years. If the man is removed, the family collapses, and then the state or anyone else can do whatever they want with the children, the woman, and the family. Pokupec agrees: "That's right, there is no protection."

To dissenters, Pokupec conveys two things. First: **one's own traumas cannot be healed by deepening the traumas of others**, that has never worked, nor will it. Second: those who believe that men are not needed in the world, he says with a dose of irony, let them wait for the first power outage or the first major potholes in the road.

He calls feminism and "leftism" in general an unserious and short-sighted political and social ideology, based on slogans that sound good at first, but make no sense as soon as one thinks more deeply about them. Nevertheless, he says he can understand an idealistic leftist in high school or at university, who is led by the heart and youthful enthusiasm, which is positive if well directed.

The problem of Croatia, according to his words, is that **it does not have a Croatian left, but a left in Croatia**. A Croatian left, according to the traditional division of political roles, would advocate for the Croatian worker, retiree, person with disabilities, and abandoned child. The left in Croatia, he says, serves other interests—globalist, "outdated, Yugoslav-nationalist", or some third ones. He does not want, he adds, to enter into "famous conspiracy theories" about Soros and Freemasonry. When the left serves interests that are anyone's except Croatian, dialogue is, he believes, difficult to achieve because the two sides do not have the well-being of the same people at heart. Some want to work for Croatia and the people in it, while others, he concludes, serve other people's interests, "consciously or unconsciously".
keywords_en: removal of the father from the family

sections.subtitle: Vjera nije privatna stvar: svjedočanstvo i zaštita nerođenih kao prvi apostolat
sections.screenshot_description: Ivan Pokupec govori da je tvrdnja kako je vjera privatna stvar perfidna podvala
sections.content:
Kruno primjećuje da se mnogi vjernici, osobito muškarci, ne žele priključiti javnim molitvama. Nekima medijski prikaz molitelja služi kao opravdanje, a drugi se jednostavno boje javno svjedočiti vjeru. Pita trebaju li se muškarci ohrabriti i javno moliti, što je i oblik evangelizacije na koju su vjernici pozvani.

Pokupec odgovara dvjema mislima iz Svetoga pisma. Prva glasi: **„Vjera se jača riječju svjedočanstva.“** Za kršćanina koji ne svjedoči pita se „čemu on služi“. Druga je poslanje Crkve, Kristove riječi: **„Idite i učinite sve narode mojim učenicima.“**

Izreku da je vjera privatna stvar naziva **„jako perfidnom podvalom“** koja je kroz kulturu, medije i politiku vrlo uspješno nametnuta. „Apsolutno ne“, kaže. Njegova privatna vjera, ističe, javna je stvar i on će je takvom i učiniti. Na svjedočenje nisu pozvani samo muškarci, nego svi vjernici, ali muškarci prvi, „u prvim redovima“.

Ponavlja da su vjernici problem stvorili sami sebi „donekle ženskom energijom“ u Katoličkoj crkvi, u kojoj se vjera poistovjećuje sa starim bakicama koje cijeli dan vrte krunicu. Mnogima, osobito u Hrvatskoj, vjera danas služi kao **skrovište**: unutar crkvenih zidova ili zidova zajednica netko je vjernik, a vani živi drugačiji život. Tako se, upozorava, ne može promijeniti ni vlastiti dom, a kamoli društvo, zemlja ili ljudi oko sebe. Vjernici su pozvani ponajprije svjedočiti svakodnevnim primjerom.

Pokupec potom iznosi svoje osobno mišljenje: **temeljni i prvi apostolat svakog vjernika jest biti za život**, odnosno zaštititi nevine, malene i nerođene. To je, kaže, odredio kao svoj prioritet broj jedan. Ako se ne zaštite nerođeni, pita, kojemu se svecu, kojim devetnicama i hodočašćima čovjek može posvetiti ako nije zaštitio „bespomoćnog nevinog“?
sections.subtitle_en: Faith is not a private matter: testimony and the protection of the unborn as the first apostolate
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Pokupec says that the claim that faith is a private matter is a perfidious deception
sections.content_en:
Kruno notes that many believers, especially men, do not want to join public prayers. For some, the media portrayal of prayer warriors serves as an excuse, while others are simply afraid to publicly witness to the faith. He asks whether men should take courage and pray publicly, which is also a form of evangelization to which believers are called.

Pokupec answers with two thoughts from Sacred Scripture. The first reads: **“Faith is strengthened by the word of testimony.”** About a Christian who does not witness, he asks "what is he good for." The second is the mission of the Church, Christ's words: **“Go therefore and make disciples of all nations.”**

He calls the saying that faith is a private matter a **“very perfidious deception”** that has been very successfully imposed through culture, media, and politics. “Absolutely not,” he says. His private faith, he emphasizes, is a public matter and he will make it so. Not only men are called to witness, but all believers, but men first, "in the front ranks."

He repeats that believers created the problem for themselves with "somewhat female energy" in the Catholic Church, in which faith is equated with old grandmas rolling the Rosary all day long. For many, especially in Croatia, faith today serves as a **hiding place**: within church walls or community walls someone is a believer, but outside lives a different life. In that way, he warns, one cannot change even one's own home, let alone society, the country, or the people around oneself. Believers are called primarily to witness by daily example.

Pokupec then presents his personal opinion: **the fundamental and first apostolate of every believer is to be for life**, that is, to protect the innocent, the little ones, and the unborn. That, he says, he determined as his number one priority. If the unborn are not protected, he asks, to which saint, to which novenas and pilgrimages can a person dedicate himself if he has not protected "the helpless innocent"?

sections.subtitle: „Bilo bi me sramota“: zavjet da nikad javno ne kritizira one koji rade za Kraljevstvo Božje
sections.screenshot_description: Ivan Pokupec objašnjava odluku da više nikad javno ne kritizira istomišljenike
sections.content:
Pokupec upozorava na problem poznat iz politike. S jedne strane raste broj **laičkih molitvenih inicijativa**, što smatra savršenim i podržava. S druge strane, među njima su počela „koškanja“: jedna inicijativa uskraćuje podršku drugoj, iako se sve bore za istu stvar. Treba biti vrlo oprezan, kaže: motivirati vjernike da se negdje uključe i nešto poduzmu, ali ne dopustiti podvalu u kojoj jedni drugima podmeću klipove pod geslom „mi smo bolji, mi smo vrijedniji, mi nećemo podržati“. Njegov je stav jasan: **„Ja podržavam sve.“** Neće reći nijednu ružnu riječ protiv ikoga tko radi na Kraljevstvu Božjem jer bi ga, kaže, bilo sramota.

Kruno potvrđuje da se u posljednje vrijeme različite molitvene zajednice i inicijative „sotoniziraju“, umjesto da se međusobno podržavaju. Druga se strana, kaže, samo smije jer nije morala ništa učiniti ni plasirati ikakvu neistinu u medijima: vjernici su se posvađali sami.

Pokupec dodaje zapažanje koje mu je, kako kaže, nedavno „sinulo“: antiteisti i ljevičari to nikad ne rade jedni drugima. Ni kada se na ljevici pojave izjave koje su, prema njegovim riječima, na granici ilegalnog, a ne samo govora mržnje, oni se međusobno neće kritizirati. Možda će prešutjeti, ali kritizirati jedni druge neće. Kruno dodaje: „pogotovo ne javno“.

Na drugoj se strani, kaže Pokupec, događa suprotno, uz poznatu šalu: „dva Hrvata, 17 stranaka“. Čim netko „izleti“, odmah se proglašava ovakvim ili onakvim. Ne prodikuje, naglašava, jer je i sam tu grešku napravio „tisuću puta“. Sada je, međutim, svjesno odlučio da to više nikada neće učiniti javno. Većinu ljudi „s naše strane“ u politici poznaje osobno i s nekima se ne slaže u 85 posto stvari, ali o njima više nikada javno neće izreći nijednu negativnu riječ. Dok jedni drugima podmeću klipove, zaključuje, druga strana ide naprijed jer je povezuju interesi, „i smiju nam se u lice“.
sections.subtitle_en: “I Would Be Ashamed”: a vow to never publicly criticize those who work for the Kingdom of God
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Pokupec explains the decision to never again publicly criticize like-minded people
sections.content_en:
Pokupec warns of a problem known from politics. On the one hand, the number of **lay prayer initiatives** is growing, which he considers perfect and supports. On the other hand, “skirmishes” have begun among them: one initiative withholds support from another, even though they are all fighting for the same thing. One needs to be very careful, he says: motivate believers to get involved somewhere and take action, but not allow the trickery in which they put spokes in each other's wheels under the slogan “we are better, we are more worthy, we will not support”. His stance is clear: **“I support everyone.”** He will not say a single bad word against anyone who works on the Kingdom of God because, he says, he would be ashamed.

Kruno confirms that recently various prayer communities and initiatives are being “demonized”, instead of supporting each other. The other side, he says, is only laughing because it did not have to do anything or place any falsehood in the media: the believers quarreled by themselves.

Pokupec adds an observation that, as he says, recently “dawned” on him: antitheists and leftists never do that to each other. Even when statements appear on the left that are, in his words, on the verge of illegal, and not just hate speech, they will not criticize each other. They might keep quiet, but they will not criticize each other. Kruno adds: “especially not publicly”.

On the other side, Pokupec says, the opposite is happening, along with the well-known joke: “two Croats, 17 parties”. As soon as someone “slips up”, they are immediately declared this or that. He is not preaching, he emphasizes, because he himself made that mistake “a thousand times”. Now, however, he has consciously decided that he will never do that publicly again. He knows most people “on our side” in politics personally and disagrees with some on 85 percent of things, but he will never again publicly utter a single negative word about them. While they put spokes in each other's wheels, he concludes, the other side moves forward because interests connect it, “and they are laughing in our faces”.
